correctness.rationale: The spherical inner-product density yields rate I(s)=-0.5 log(1-s^2). Distinct unordered edges have pairwise-independent inner products, so angular-bin counts concentrate whenever their expected counts are exponential. Finite-bin upper and lower bounds establish the constrained Laplace limit. The identity (1+rho^2-2rho s)-(1-s^2)=(s-rho)^2 and derivative determine its sharp threshold; a tilted, truncated pair-sum has mean tending to one and variance tending to zero above that threshold. Exact Poisson-semigroup convolution gives the already-known finite variance and the second threshold. Reproduced 2,566 numerical/algebraic assertions from the embedded checker; the infinite proof is not based on numerical enumeration. Critical first-threshold probability and second-threshold distribution remain unproved.
